questions.text: With a remote check every 60 minutes, the batteries last about 13 months with ordinary Wi-Fi firmware: more than 1 year, but with a thin safety margin (9 % instead of 15 %). How do we keep a comfortable margin?
options: (recommended) Require fast-reconnect firmware (remembers the network, resumes the secure session): about 15 months, no extra cost, measured on the first prototype
Accept about 13 months with ordinary firmware and the thinner margin
Check every 70 minutes instead of 60: about 14 months with ordinary firmware, commands can take up to 70 minutes
Add a tiny low-power helper chip that does the minute-by-minute control: about 16 months even with ordinary firmware, +1 USD and a second firmware to write
questions.why: Conflict C6: 1 year with 15 % margin allows 80 uA average; the budget is 85 uA at 60 uAh per Wi-Fi check-in, 75 uA at 50 uAh.

questions.text: What should happen to the heating when the batteries run out?
options: (recommended) Shortly before the batteries are empty, the device switches both rooms OFF, sends a 'battery empty' message and stops. If someone pulls the batteries while a room is heating, that room stays ON until new batteries go in (the label already says to switch off the heating breaker first). No extra cost
Both rooms switch OFF even if the batteries are pulled out suddenly: needs a large energy-storage part, about +1.5 USD, a slightly shorter battery life (about 2-5 %) and a taller part on the board
Shortly before the batteries are empty, switch both rooms ON (keeps the rooms warm, wastes heating) instead of OFF
questions.why: Conflict C7: switching both relays off from stored energy alone needs a 22-33 mF supercapacitor; a firmware cut-off at 2.0 V uses the cells instead (3.7 uAh).

questions.text: How accurate must the room temperature reading be (the electronics only; the probe itself adds its own error)?
options: (recommended) Within 0.3 C, guaranteed by design: adds a small precision measuring chip, about +1.5 USD; we confirm the total stays under 25 USD when parts are priced
Within 0.3 C, but each unit calibrated once on a test jig: no extra cost, accuracy only proven by measuring every unit, behaviour over temperature less certain
Within about 1 C: no extra cost, no calibration
questions.why: Conflict C8: the Wi-Fi chip's own ADC gives +-0.95 C; an external 16-bit ADC gives +-0.07 C.

questions.text: The only small relays with the safety insulation we need use slightly more energy per switch than planned (7-9 mJ instead of 5 mJ). This costs about 0.25 % of battery life. Is that acceptable?
options: (recommended) Yes: keep the full switching pulse for reliable switching even with old or cold relays; about 1 day less battery life per year, no cost
No: shorten the pulse to stay at 5 mJ, with less safety margin for reliable switching
Search for another relay: may be taller (size) or more expensive
questions.why: Conflict C9: Panasonic ADW1103HLW 45 ohm coil, 30 ms pulse = 7.2 mJ nominal, 8.5 mJ worst case; +0.2 uA average.
